/-!
# Conjecture 4.48

by A. Yu. Olshanskii

A locally finite group is said to be an $A$-group if all of its Sylow subgroups are
abelian. Does every variety of $A$-groups possess a finite basis of identities?

Here an identity (law) is a word $w$ in the free group on countably many letters
$x_0, x_1, \dots$; a group $G$ satisfies $w$ if $w$ evaluates to $1$ under every substitution
of elements of $G$ for the letters. A variety of groups is the class of all groups satisfying
a given set $W$ of identities, and it possesses a finite basis of identities if it is also
defined by some finite set of identities. A variety of $A$-groups is a variety all of whose
members are $A$-groups. Sylow $p$-subgroups of a (possibly infinite) locally finite group are
its maximal $p$-subgroups, which is Mathlib's `Sylow p G`.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

letters $x_0, x_1, \dots$, if `w` evaluates to `1` under every substitution of elements of `G`

justification.closest_existing_considered: FreeGroup.lift / MonoidHom from FreeGroup (used as building blocks); no existing predicate for 'G satisfies the law w'.

blocks.name: SatisfiesIdentity

/-- A group `G` satisfies the identity (law) `w`, a word in the free group on the countably many
letters $x_0, x_1, \dots$, if `w` evaluates to `1` under every substitution of elements of `G`
for the letters, i.e. under every homomorphism from the free group to `G`. -/
def SatisfiesIdentity (G : Type*) [Group G] (w : FreeGroup ℕ) : Prop :=

blocks.docstring: A group is locally finite if every finitely generated subgroup is finite.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Monoid.IsTorsion (too weak: torsion ≠ locally finite), LocallyFiniteOrder (unrelated), Group.FG/Subgroup.FG (used as building block).

claims.decomposer_note: Single unlettered yes/no question (Prop: every group variety all of whose members are A-groups, i.e. locally finite groups with all Sylow — maximal p- — subgroups abelian, is finitely based); the preceding sentence only defines 'A-group' and poses no question, and such a variety is necessarily locally finite of finite exponent, so 'variety of A-groups' should be read as a variety every member of which is an A-group (equivalently, whose finite groups have abelian Sylow subgroups).
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the same (correct) reading: a variety is the class of all groups satisfying a set W of laws in FreeGroup ℕ; 'variety of A-groups' means every model of W is locally finite (every f.g. subgroup finite) with every Sylow p-subgroup (Mathlib's maximal p-subgroup, p prime) abelian; 'finite basis' means a finite set B of laws with exactly the same models; answer(True) = positive answer. Checked: primality restriction on p is present (IsPGroup 0 would force abelian), the hypothesis is non-vacuous (trivial variety, var(S_3), abelian groups of exponent n qualify; the variety of all groups does not), and quantifying over Type-0 groups loses nothing (equality of varieties is detected on the countable relatively free group FreeGroup ℕ / W(F); failure of local finiteness or of abelian Sylow subgroups is witnessed by a countable f.g. subgroup which is itself a model). c06 chosen as base because it is clean, uses the standard 'word w = 1' form of laws, has thorough docstrings, and includes proved @[category API] tests for the bespoke definitions as CONTRIBUTING requires; c01/c02/c07/c08 lack such tests, c04 is needlessly elaborate (class-of-groups predicate) and has over-long lines, c03/c05 are equally faithful alternatives. My edits: wrapped one >100-char line (twice) and made the Finset→Set coercion explicit (↑B). Compiles with only the 'declaration uses sorry' warning.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 4.48

by A. Yu. Olshanskii

A locally finite group is said to be an $A$-group if all of its Sylow subgroups are
abelian. Does every variety of $A$-groups possess a finite basis of identities?

Here an identity (law) is a word $w$ in the free group on countably many letters
$x_0, x_1, \dots$; a group $G$ satisfies $w$ if $w$ evaluates to $1$ under every substitution
of elements of $G$ for the letters. A variety of groups is the class of all groups satisfying
a given set $W$ of identities, and it possesses a finite basis of identities if it is also
defined by some finite set of identities. A variety of $A$-groups is a variety all of whose
members are $A$-groups. Sylow $p$-subgroups of a (possibly infinite) locally finite group are
its maximal $p$-subgroups, which is Mathlib's `Sylow p G`.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«4.48»

/-- A group `G` satisfies the identity (law) `w`, a word in the free group on the countably many
letters $x_0, x_1, \dots$, if `w` evaluates to `1` under every substitution of elements of `G`
for the letters, i.e. under every homomorphism from the free group to `G`. -/
def SatisfiesIdentity (G : Type*) [Group G] (w : FreeGroup ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ φ : FreeGroup ℕ →* G, φ w = 1

/-- The variety of groups defined by a set `W` of identities is the class of all groups
satisfying every identity in `W`. `MemVariety W G` says that `G` belongs to this variety. -/
def MemVariety (W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ w ∈ W, SatisfiesIdentity G w

/-- A group is locally finite if every finitely generated subgroup is finite. -/
def IsLocallyFinite (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → Finite H

/-- A locally finite group is an $A$-group if all of its Sylow subgroups are abelian, where a
Sylow `p`-subgroup (`p` prime) is a maximal `p`-subgroup. -/
def IsAGroup (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  IsLocallyFinite G ∧ ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → ∀ P : Sylow p G, IsMulCommutative P

/-- Every finite group is locally finite. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
lemma IsLocallyFinite.of_finite (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite G] : IsLocallyFinite G :=
  fun _ _ => inferInstance

/-- Every finite abelian group is an $A$-group. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
lemma IsAGroup.of_finite_of_isMulCommutative (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite G]
    [IsMulCommutative G] : IsAGroup G :=
  ⟨.of_finite G, fun _ _ _ => inferInstance⟩

/-- Abelian groups satisfy the commutator identity $[x_0, x_1] = 1$. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
lemma satisfiesIdentity_commutator (G : Type*) [Group G] [IsMulCommutative G] :
    SatisfiesIdentity G ⁅FreeGroup.of 0, FreeGroup.of 1⁆ := fun φ => by
  rw [map_commutatorElement, commutatorElement_eq_one_iff_mul_comm]
  exact mul_comm _ _

/-- A variety defined by a finite set of identities possesses a finite basis of identities. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
lemma exists_finset_memVariety_iff_of_finite (W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) (hW : W.Finite) :
    ∃ B : Finset (FreeGroup ℕ),
      ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], MemVariety W G ↔ MemVariety ↑B G :=
  ⟨hW.toFinset, fun _ _ => by simp [MemVariety]⟩

/--
A locally finite group is said to be an $A$-group if all of its Sylow subgroups are abelian.
Does every variety of $A$-groups possess a finite basis of identities?

That is: for every set $W$ of identities such that every group satisfying all identities in $W$
is an $A$-group, is there a finite set $B$ of identities such that a group satisfies all
identities in $W$ if and only if it satisfies all identities in $B$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«4.48» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ),
      (∀ (G : Type) [Group G], MemVariety W G → IsAGroup G) →
      ∃ B : Finset (FreeGroup ℕ),
        ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], MemVariety W G ↔ MemVariety ↑B G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«4.48»

items: A 'variety' is represented by an arbitrary set W of identities (words in FreeGroup ℕ, i.e. in countably many letters); V(W) is the class of groups satisfying all w ∈ W. This is the standard (H. Neumann) definition; by Birkhoff's theorem it agrees with the S/H/P-closed-class definition, and every variety arises from some W (e.g. its full set of laws).
An identity w holds in G iff φ w = 1 for every homomorphism φ : FreeGroup ℕ →* G (equivalently every substitution of elements of G for the letters).

'Possesses a finite basis of identities' is formalized as: there is a finite set B of identities with V(B) = V(W) as classes of groups. If V(B) = V(W) then B is automatically a set of laws of V(W), so this is equivalent to 'the laws of V(W) all follow from finitely many of them'.
'Variety of A-groups' is read (as directed by the decomposition table) as a variety all of whose members are A-groups, expressed as ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], MemVariety W G → IsAGroup G.

A-group: IsLocallyFinite G (every finitely generated subgroup is finite) ∧ for every PRIME p, every Sylow p-subgroup (Mathlib's `Sylow p G`, i.e. maximal p-subgroup — the usual meaning of Sylow subgroup for locally finite groups) is abelian (IsMulCommutative). Restricting to prime p avoids the degenerate/stronger readings of IsPGroup for p = 0, 1 or composite p.

Groups are quantified over `Type` (universe 0), following Kourovka/1_40.lean. This is mathematically harmless: membership in a variety, local finiteness, and the existence of a non-abelian maximal p-subgroup are all detected by countable (finitely generated) subgroups, which have isomorphic copies in Type.

Four short `category API` lemmas with real proofs are included as sanity tests of the bespoke definitions (finite groups are locally finite; finite abelian groups are A-groups; abelian groups satisfy [x₀,x₁]; a finitely axiomatized variety trivially has a finite basis).

reviewer_notes: Single-slot problem; no candidate omitted it and all compile. Modeling choices a reviewer should know: (1) 'variety of A-groups' is read as a variety all of whose members are A-groups (the decomposition-table reading; the alternative 'generated by A-groups' would admit e.g. the variety of all abelian groups, which is not locally finite, and does not match the notebook's definition of A-group as a locally finite group). (2) Sylow subgroups of a possibly infinite locally finite group are its maximal p-subgroups, which is exactly Mathlib's `Sylow p G` (no finiteness or Fact p.Prime needed); p is restricted to primes. (3) Laws are words in FreeGroup ℕ (countably many letters suffice since each law uses finitely many); the finite basis B is not required to be a subset of W, which is the standard notion (V(B)=V(W) forces B ⊆ laws of V(W)). (4) Groups are quantified over `Type` following the Kourovka files' convention; this is provably equivalent to quantifying over all universes for this statement. `answer(sorry)` printing as `True` in #print is the repository elaborator's documented default, not an issue.
